hints.content: To translate $\triangle ABC$ using $(x,y)\to(x -6,y -7)$, we basically translate $\triangle ABC$'s vertices and connect them.

For example, point $\blueD{A(4,4)}$ is translated to $(4 -6,4 -7)=\greenD{(-2,-3)}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a triangle with vertices A B C and Vertex C at two, two, vertex B at seven, zero, and vertex A at four, four. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves from vertex A six units left and seven units down to a point at negative two, negative three.

hints.content:
Doing this for all vertices and connecting them, we get the following mapping:



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with a triangle with vertices A B C and Vertex C at two, two, vertex B at seven, zero, and vertex A at four, four. The x- and y- axes scale by one. A dashed line moves from the three vertices six units left and seven units down to form the image of a congruent triangle with vertices at negative two, negative three, negative four, negative five, and one, negative seven.
